nodes.name: Definition 2.1: Locally-compact Hausdorff nilspaces Def
Definition 5.5, Definition 5.8: Groupable congruences fiber transitive filtrations Defs
nodes.statement:
Let $\mathrm{X}$ be a nilspace. A \emph{groupable congruence} on $\mathrm{X}$ is an equivalence relation $\sim$ on $\mathrm{X}$ that satisfies the following property:
\begin{eqnarray}
&\textrm{for every $i\geq 0$, for all $x,y\in \mathrm{X}$ such that $x\sim y$ and $\pi_i(x)=\pi_i(y)$,}& \\
&\textrm{there exists $g\in \Theta(\mathrm{X})^{(\sim)}\cap \Theta_{i+1}(\mathrm{X})$ such that $g\,x=y$.}&
\end{eqnarray}

Let $\mathrm{X}$ be a nilspace and let $G_\bullet$ be a subfiltration of $\Theta_\bullet(\mathrm{X})$. We say that $G_\bullet$ is a \emph{fiber-transitive filtration on} $\mathrm{X}$ (or that $(G,G_\bullet)$ is a \emph{fiber-transitive} filtered group on $\mathrm{X}$) 
if it satisfies property (15). A subgroup $\Gamma$ of $\Theta(\mathrm{X})$ will be said to be \emph{fiber-transitive on} $\mathrm{X}$ if the filtration $(\Gamma\cap \Theta_i(\mathrm{X}))_{i\geq 0}$ is fiber-transitive on $\mathrm{X}$.

nodes.name: Theorem 2.9: Basics Thm
nodes.statement: Let $\mathrm{X}$ be an \textsc{lch} $k$-step nilspace. Then $\mathrm{X}_{k-1}$, equipped with the cube sets $(\pi_{k-1}^{\llbracket n\rrbracket}(\mathrm{C}^n(\mathrm{X})))_{n\ge 0}$, is a $(k-1)$-step \textsc{lch} nilspace with respect to the quotient topology.

nodes.name: Definition 2.19: Lie-fibered nilspaces Def
nodes.statement: Let $\mathrm{X}$ be a $k$-step \textsc{lch} nilspace. We say that $\mathrm{X}$ is a \emph{locally-compact and finite-rank} nilspace, or \emph{Lie-fibered nilspace}, if all its structure groups are compactly generated (abelian) Lie groups.

nodes.name: Definition 2.26, Proposition 2.32: Extensions Def lifts of translations Prop
nodes.statement:
Let $k,t\ge 0$ be integers. Let $\mathrm{X}$, $\mathrm{Y}$ be $k$-step \textsc{lch} nilspaces such that $\mathrm{Y}$ is an algebraic nilspace extension of $\mathrm{X}$ of degree $t$, by some \textsc{lch} abelian group $\mathrm{Z}$, with associated projection $p:\mathrm{Y}\rightarrow\mathrm{X}$. We say that $\mathrm{Y}$ (or $p:\mathrm{Y}\rightarrow \mathrm{X}$) is a \emph{continuous extension} of $\mathrm{X}$ if $\mathrm{Y}$ is additionally an \textsc{lch} abelian $\mathrm{Z}$-bundle with base $\mathrm{X}$.

Let $\mathrm{X}$ be a $k$-step \textsc{lch} nilspace, let $i<k$, and let $\alpha\in\Theta_i(\mathrm{X}_{k-1})$ be a (continuous) translation. Suppose that there is a continuous nilspace morphism $m:\mathrm{X}_{k-1}\rightarrow \mathcal{T}_{k-1}$ such that $\pi\circ\hspace{-0.02 cm} m=\mathrm{id}_{\mathrm{X}_{k-1}}$ (where $\pi$ is the projection $\mathcal{T}_{k-1}\rightarrow\mathrm{X}_{k-1}$). Then there exists a continuous translation $\beta\in\Theta_i(\mathrm{X})$ such that $\pi_{k-1}\circ\hspace{-0.02 cm} \beta(x) = \alpha\circ\hspace{-0.02 cm} \pi_{k-1}(x)$ for all $x\in \mathrm{X}$.

nodes.name: Lemma 5.12, Lemma 5.13: Algebraic aspects Lems
nodes.statement:
If $H_\bullet$ is a fiber-transitive filtration on a $k$-step nilspace $\mathrm{X}$, then for every $j\ge 0$ the filtration $\eta_j(H_\bullet):=(\eta_j(H_i))_{i\ge 0}$ is fiber-transitive on $\mathrm{X}_j$. Equivalently, every groupable congruence $\sim$ on $\mathrm{X}$ induces a groupable congruence $\sim_{(j)}$ on $\mathrm{X}_j$ defined by $\pi_j(x)\sim_{(j)}\pi_j(y) \Leftrightarrow \exists x'\sim x$, $\pi_j(x')=\pi_j(y)$.

Let $\mathrm{X}$ be a $k$-step nilspace, with structure groups $\mathrm{Z}_i$, $i\in [k]$, and let $H_\bullet$ be a fiber-transitive filtration on $\mathrm{X}$. Then for each $i\in[k]$ the $i$-th structure group of $\pi_H(\mathrm{X})$ is $\mathrm{Z}_i/\eta_i(H_i)$. Moreover, for every $n\geq 0$, for each $\mathrm{c}\in\mathrm{C}^n(\mathrm{X})$ the group $\mathrm{C}^n(H_\bullet)$ acts transitively on $\{\mathrm{c}'\in\mathrm{C}^n(\mathrm{X}): \pi_H \circ\hspace{-0.02 cm} \mathrm{c}' = \pi_H \circ\hspace{-0.02 cm} \mathrm{c}\}$.

nodes.name: Definition 5.22, Theorem 5.35: Topological aspects Def Thm
nodes.statement: Let $\mathrm{X}$ be a $k$-step Lie-fibered nilspace, and let $H_\bullet$ be a closed fiber-transitive filtration on $\mathrm{X}$. Then $\pi_H(\mathrm{X})$ equipped with the quotient topology is a $k$-step  Lie-fibered nilspace.

nodes.name: Theorem 2.21: Open mapping Thm
nodes.statement: Let $\mathrm{X}$,$\mathrm{Y}$ be Lie-fibered $k$-step nilspaces, and let $\varphi:\mathrm{X}\rightarrow\mathrm{Y}$ be a continuous fibration. Then $\varphi$ is an open map.

nodes.name: Theorem 2.40: $\Theta(\mathrm{X})$ is Polish Thm
nodes.statement: Let $\mathrm{X}$ be a $k$-step Lie-fibered nilspace. Then for every $i\in [k]$ the translation group $\Theta_i(\mathrm{X})$ is a Polish group.

nodes.name: Theorem 3.11: Lifting Thm
nodes.statement: Let $A=Z\times \mathbb{T}^s$ be a compact\footnote{The assumption of compactness can be relaxed to that of being compactly-generated, using similar arguments.} abelian Lie group, let $B=\mathbb{Z}^r\times \mathbb{R}^s$ be the covering group and $\pi:B\rightarrow A$ the covering homomorphism. Then for any free nilspace $F$, any $k\in \mathbb{N}$ and any $\phi\in \hom(F,\mathcal{D}_k(A))$, there exists $\psi\in\hom(F,\mathcal{D}_k(B))$ such that $\phi = \pi\circ\hspace{-0.02 cm} \psi$.

nodes.name: Lemma A.3, Theorem 3.15: Description of $\hom(F,F')$ Lem $\Theta(F)$ is Lie Thm
Theorem 4.1: Extensions of free nilspaces are split extensions Thm
nodes.statement: Let $F$ be a $k$-step free nilspace and let $\mathrm{Y}$ be a degree-$k$ extension of $F$ by an abelian Lie group $\mathrm{Z}$, with corresponding fibration $q:\mathrm{Y}\rightarrow F$. Then this  extension splits, i.e., there exists a continuous morphism $s:F\rightarrow\mathrm{Y}$ such that $q\circ\hspace{-0.02 cm} s=\mathrm{id}$. In particular $\mathrm{Y}$ is isomorphic as an \textsc{lch} nilspace to the product-nilspace $F\times \mathcal{D}_k(\mathrm{Z})$.

nodes.name: Theorem 6.1: cfr nilspaces are quotients of free nilspaces Thm
nodes.statement: Let $\mathrm{X}$ be a $k$-step \textsc{cfr} nilspace. Then there exists a $k$-step free nilspace $F$ and a closed groupable congruence $\sim$ on $F$ such that $\pi_\sim(F)$, $\mathrm{X}$ are isomorphic as \textsc{cfr} nilspaces.

nodes.name: Definition 5.40, Proposition 5.46: Free groupable congruences Def Prop
nodes.statement: Let $F$ be a $k$-step free nilspace, and let $H_\bullet$ be a free fiber-transitive filtration on $F$ that is finitely-generated, fiber-discrete, and such that $\pi_H(F)$ is a compact nilspace. Then there exists a toral nilspace $\mathrm{X}$ and a continuous injective morphism from $\pi_H(F)$ into $\mathrm{X}$.

nodes.name: Lemma 7.3: Double-coset nilspaces Lem
nodes.statement:
Let $(G,G_\bullet)$ be a filtered group of finite degree $k$. Let $K,\Gamma$ be subgroups of $G$. The following statements are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=0.7cm]
    \item The filtration $\Gamma_\bullet:=(\Gamma\cap G_i)_{i\ge 0}$ is fiber-transitive on the coset nilspace $K\backslash G$.
    \item For any $x\in G$ and all $i\ge 0$ we have $(Kx\Gamma)\cap(KxG_i)=Kx(\Gamma\cap G_i)$.
\end{enumerate}

nodes.name: Theorem 7.16: New proof of the inverse from J T for the $U^3$ -norm Thm
nodes.statement: Let $\epsilon>0$, let $\mathrm{Z}$ be a finite abelian group. Let $f:\mathrm{Z}\rightarrow \mathbb{C}$ be a 1-bounded function with $\|f\|_{U^{3}(\mathrm{Z})}\ge \epsilon$. Then there exists a degree-2 connected nilmanifold $G/\Gamma$ drawn from some finite collection $\mathcal{N}_\epsilon$ of such manifolds (where each such nilmanifold is  endowed with an arbitrary compatible metric), a $O_\epsilon(1)$-Lipschitz function $F:G/\Gamma\rightarrow \mathbb{C}$ and a nilspace morphism $\phi:\mathcal{D}_1(\mathrm{Z})\rightarrow G/\Gamma$, such that $|\mathbb{E}_{x\in \mathrm{Z}} f(x) \overline{F(\phi(x))}|\gg_{\epsilon} 1$.

nodes.name: Theorem 1.15: $k$ -step compact nilspaces as double coset spaces Thm
nodes.statement: Let $\mathrm{X}$ be a $k$-step compact nilspace. There exists a $k$-step pro-free nilspace $F$, a pro-Lie subgroup $G$ of $\Theta(F)$, and a fiber-transitive group $\Gamma\subset G$ such that, letting $K:=\mathrm{Stab}_G(x_0)=\{\alpha\in G:\alpha(x_0)=x_0\}$ for some $x_0\in \mathrm{X}$, we have that $\mathrm{X}$ is isomorphic as a compact nilspace to $K\backslash G/\Gamma$.

nodes.name: Theorem 1.17, Theorem 1.19: Inverse with double-coset spaces Thm with higher-order lattice actions T…
nodes.statement:
There exists a family of double-coset nilspaces $\mathcal{N}$, such that for any metrization $D$ of $\mathcal{N}$ the following holds. For any  $\epsilon>0$ and $k\in\mathbb{N}$,  there exists $M_{k,\epsilon}>0$ such that for any finite abelian group $\mathrm{Z}$ and any 1-bounded  function $f:\mathrm{Z}\rightarrow \mathbb{C}$  with $\|f\|_{U^{k+1}(\mathrm{Z})}\ge \epsilon$, for some $i\leq M_{k,\epsilon}$ the triple $(G,K,\Gamma)_{k,i}$ in $\mathcal{N}$  satisfies the following:
\setlength{\leftmargini}{0.7cm}
\begin{enumerate}
    \item there is a polynomial map $g\in \hom(\mathcal{D}_1(\mathbb{Z}^n),G_\bullet)$ such that, letting $\pi_{K,\Gamma}:G\rightarrow K\backslash G/\Gamma$ be the quotient map and $\varphi:\mathbb{Z}^n\rightarrow\mathrm{Z}$ be the natural surjective homomorphism, there exists a morphism $m:\mathcal{D}_1(\mathrm{Z})\rightarrow K\backslash G/\Gamma$ with $\pi_{K,\Gamma}\circ\hspace{-0.02 cm} g = m\circ\hspace{-0.02 cm} \varphi$,
    \item there is a continuous function $F:K\backslash G/\Gamma\rightarrow \mathbb{C}$ with Lipschitz norm $O_{k,\epsilon}(1)$,
\end{enumerate}
and letting $D\subset \mathbb{Z}^n$ be any fundamental domain of $\mathbb{Z}^n/\ker(\varphi)$, we have
\[
\left|\mathbb{E}_{x\in D} f(x) \overline{F\left(K g(x) \Gamma\right)}\right|\gg_{k,\epsilon} 1.
\]

There exists a family of higher-order lattice actions $\mathcal{M}$, such that for any metrization $D$ of $\mathcal{M}$ the following holds.
For any $\epsilon>0$ and $k\in\mathbb{N}$, there exists $N_{k,\epsilon}>0$ such that for any finite abelian group $\mathrm{Z}$  and any 1-bounded function $f:\mathrm{Z}\rightarrow \mathbb{C}$ with $\|f\|_{U^{k+1}(\mathrm{Z})}\ge \epsilon$, for some $i\leq N_{k,\epsilon}$ the pair $(F,\Gamma)_{i,k}$ in $\mathcal{M}$ satisfies the following:
\setlength{\leftmargini}{0.7cm}
\begin{enumerate}
    \item there is a polynomial map $g:\mathbb{Z}^n\rightarrow F$ such that, letting $\pi_{\Gamma}:F\rightarrow F/\Gamma$ be the quotient fibration and $\varphi:\mathbb{Z}^n\rightarrow\mathrm{Z}$ be the natural surjective homomorphism, there exists a morphism $m:\mathcal{D}_1(\mathrm{Z})\rightarrow F/\Gamma$ with $\pi_{\Gamma}\circ\hspace{-0.02 cm} g = m\circ\hspace{-0.02 cm} \varphi$,
    \item there is a continuous function $\phi:F/\Gamma\rightarrow \mathbb{C}$ with Lipschitz norm $O_{k,\epsilon}(1)$,
\end{enumerate}
and letting $D\subset \mathbb{Z}^n$ be any fundamental domain of $\mathbb{Z}^n/\ker(\varphi)$, we have
\[
\left|\mathbb{E}_{x\in D} f(x) \overline{\phi(\pi_\Gamma(g(x)))}\right|\gg_{k,\epsilon} 1.
\]
